messages.content: Predict a human choice in an online modified dictator game. The participant chooses between allocation buttons A and B. Each option allocates experimental coins to the participant (self) and a passive charity (charity); the charity cannot reject it or take a counteraction. In the complete-information section both amounts are displayed, one option gives 5 coins each and the other varies; each totals 10 coins. Read the current A/B amounts, since A does not always mean equal or more generous. In the incomplete-information section both self amounts are shown, but BOTH charity amounts initially appear as question marks. Participants were told there is a 50% chance the total is 10 coins and a 50% chance it is a random amount, fixed before the trial. This concerns hidden amounts, not a 50% chance of payment. Its random distribution was not specified. Never replace a hidden charity amount by 10 minus self, or assume it is 5. First choose REVEAL to see the charity amounts, or DECIDE to move to allocation while leaving them hidden. Revealing has no monetary fee or bonus penalty. Then choose A or B; DECIDE is not an allocation, an opt-out or a refusal to donate. One completed allocation trial is randomly selected for implementation at the end. Its self coins become a real euro bonus and charity coins a real donation. A fixed participation payment is separate; the supplied participant instructions do not give the exact conversion rate or maximum bonus. Coins are not euros, cents, percentages or probabilities. Before the game the participant rated five charity categories from 1 (not at all important) to 7 (extremely important), ranked all five, and completed eight word-association filler trials. The current charity is the personally most important (rank 1) or least important (rank 5); least important does not imply disliked or unimportant. Category codes are DOG = dog rescue and re-housing; EDUCATION = education in disadvantaged communities; ENVIRONMENT = environmental protection; MENTAL_HEALTH = mental health helpline; HOMELESS = support for homeless people. Profile gender Male/Female is the original self-report. The profile importance object gives the five earlier ratings and ranking lists categories from most to least important. The current object identifies the event and visible options. The history lines contain only earlier real game events: event and trial are ordinal positions, task is information_choice or allocation_choice, charity and rank identify the recipient category and prior preference, information is complete or hidden, prior_information_action is the earlier same-trial REVEAL/DECIDE when applicable, options contains self/charity coin pairs and action is that earlier response. null means an amount remains hidden or an information step does not apply, as specified by its field. Earlier hidden charity amounts stay hidden unless that earlier trial was revealed. Selecting an allocation itself does not reveal its hidden charity amounts or the eventual payout. Current reaction time, current answer, future choices and terminal payment records are not supplied. Guided walkthroughs are instructed exercises and are not free decisions in this history. Predict the participant's recorded choice without explaining or prescribing a socially desirable response. Current target: choose an allocation at the current visible information state. Output only A or B.
